subject: Dedicated capacity pricing qualification
messages:
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Laura Thompson <laura.thompson@finserv.com>
Date: 2026-03-29T16:15:00-07:00
Subject: Post-call: dedicated capacity pricing qualification

Hi Laura — thanks for the call today. Quick recap and a couple follow-ups so we can size Dedicated capacity and get you a concrete reserved pricing proposal.

Recap (from our discovery):
- Primary workload: document understanding + multi-turn chat for customer support (mostly extractive + short generation).
- Typical request: ~512 tokens (including context + response) on average, peak flows up to ~2k tokens for longer threads.
- Expected steady-state volume: ~15M tokens/day (avg) with spikes to ~30M on billing cycles; ~12 concurrent QPS peak today.
- Security: must be deployed in dedicated Redwood capacity (VPC) — SOC2 plus vendor questionnaire in progress.

Specific asks so we size the reserved config:
1) Confirm target committed monthly budget range (you mentioned $10k–$20k/mo as a ballpark) — is that monthly or per team?
2) Any hard requirement on GPU family? (You said H100 preference on the call; we can size on H100 or A100 equivalently for pricing.)
3) Target latency/throughput SLOs (p50/p95 target token latency or reqs/sec)?

What I’ll send next: a preliminary pricing sheet with 2 config options (2x and 4x reserved GPUs), estimated throughput (tokens/sec and reqs/sec for 512-token avg), and modeled unit economics (approx $/1M tokens) for committed discounts vs on-demand. Also the mutual action plan and a link to the SOC2 + vendor pack.

If that looks right, can you confirm answers to items 1–3 above and loop in procurement (Tom Nguyen) if you want us to include standard purchasing timelines/PO steps?

Thanks — I'll draft the first pricing options and have Rishi (our SE) join the follow-up call to review throughput/benchmarks.

—
Vanessa Ortiz
Account Executive, Redwood Inference
vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com | (415) 555-0198

Date: 2026-03-29T17:02:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: dedicated capacity pricing qualification

Thanks Vanessa — appreciate the recap. A few answers inline.

> 1) Confirm target committed monthly budget range
We were talking team-wide — $10k–$20k/month is our initial target for the first year. If committed pricing gets us to <$15k/mo for our current volume that would be attractive.

> 2) GPU family requirement
Prefer H100 (we want the higher memory and perf headroom). Open to A100 if pricing is meaningfully better, but H100 is the default.

> 3) Target latency/throughput SLOs
We'd like p95 token latency under 200ms for typical short requests (<512 tokens) and throughput to support current peaks ~12 QPS with headroom to 25 QPS for seasonal spikes.

Additional context:
- Average request length today ~512 tokens, but 10–15% of requests can be 1k–2k tokens.
- Monthly committed token volume target for year 1: ~450M tokens/mo (15M/day * 30).
- Procurement: looping Tom (procurement) on the thread to coordinate contract and vendor evaluation items.

We attached our vendor requirements doc for reference.

Thanks — happy to review the pricing sheet tomorrow or early next week.

—
Laura Thompson
Head of ML Products, FinServ Analytics
laura.thompson@finserv.com
From: Vanessa Ortiz <vanessa.ortiz@redwood.com>
To: Laura Thompson <laura.thompson@finserv.com>
Cc: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>, Tom Nguyen <tom.nguyen@finserv.com>
Date: 2026-03-30T09:30:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Post-call: dedicated capacity pricing qualification

Laura — thanks for the fast turnaround and the vendor doc. Attaching a preliminary pricing sheet and a mutual action plan (see attachments). High-level notes below so you have the numbers for procurement.

Sizing assumptions we used to build the configs:
- Avg request = 512 tokens
- Avg tokens/day = 15M (450M/mo committed)
- Peak concurrency target ~25 QPS headroom (to cover spikes)
- Mixed request lengths: 85% <512 tokens, 15% 1k–2k tokens

Option A — Balanced (Recommended for your stated budget target):
- Hardware: 2x H100 80GB reserved (dedicated pool)
- Estimated steady throughput: ~18–22M tokens/min (300–370k tokens/sec aggregated) depending on batching and KV cache hit rates; supports ~25 QPS for 512-token avg with moderate batching.
- Modeled cost (committed reserved discount applied): ~ $12,000/month (covers infra + runtime + management).
- Unit economics: ~ $16–$18 per 1M tokens (modeled; depends on exact cache hit and batching).
- Notes: Good latency profile; lower capital commitment than 4x.

Option B — Throughput-first (for aggressive peak/headroom):
- Hardware: 4x A100/H100 equivalent (we price A100 variant slightly lower)
- Estimated steady throughput: ~40–50M tokens/min; comfortable supporting 50+ QPS at 512-token avg with less batching needed.
- Modeled cost: ~ $22,500/month (committed reserved pricing).

- Unit economics: ~ $10–$14 per 1M tokens at higher utilization; better $/1M with scale.

Important unit economics notes:
- Our modeled $/1M tokens assumes committed reserved capacity and typical KV caching. On-demand runs (no commit) can be 2x–3x higher per 1M tokens.
- Quantization and model variant selection (e.g., 4-bit quant vs FP16; smaller distilled variants) can materially change $/1M — we can model specifics if you share target quality/regression budgets.

Next steps I propose:
1) Internal alignment: confirm preferred option (A or B) or ask us to size a middle-ground (3x).
2) Deep-dive with Rishi to validate throughput numbers against your test prompts and p95 latency targets — 60 min session.
3) Procurement: we’ll produce a draft SOW and pricing quote after the deep-dive.

I attached: redwood_dedicated_pricing_sheet_v2.xlsx and mutual_action_plan.docx. Let us know available times for the deep-dive (Rishi & I can do 11–1pm PT tomorrow or Thursday morning).

—
Vanessa Ortiz

Thanks Vanessa — this is super helpful. We’d like to proceed with Option A as the baseline (2x H100) to match our budget target, and keep Option B as an expansion path.

Procurement (Tom) requested a 60-minute technical deep-dive with Rishi to validate throughput on our representative prompt set and to confirm the SLOs — tomorrow 11:30am PT works for Tom and me. I’ve accepted the tentative calendar hold.

Next asks for Redwood before the call:
- A short test harness or set of benchmarking prompts (we’ll run client-side if needed).
- Draft SOW and pricing quote (high level) to circulate internally — we need the cost line items to review before procurement route.

I attached the vendor requirements (see previous). After the deep-dive, if the throughput looks good we’ll move to a PO for a 12-month reserved commitment.
